explanation: King Solomon of Israel, who is believed to be the author of Song of Songs and son of King David.
The woman loved by the man in Song of Songs, often representing God's people or the church.
The man who loves the bride in Song of Songs, often symbolizing God or Jesus Christ.
A deep devotion and feeling between two people, here between the bride and groom.
The act of looking for something or someone, in this case the bride's search for her beloved.
The time of day when it is dark outside, used here as a metaphor for uncertainty and trials.
The time of day when it is light outside, used here as a metaphor for joy and reunion.
People who protect and guard the city; in Song of Songs they help the bride find her beloved.
A tree symbolizing victory, triumph, and eternal life, used in Song of Songs as an image of love and unity.
